question: Does B0's per-budget advantage over A0 in V1a survive when the cascade uses as many network calls per candidate as B0 (A0 with 25 event + 25 geometry steps)?

reused_arms.A0-50+50: sealed V1a A0 streams (screen/efficiency_s{seed}), not re-run
reused_arms.B0-50: sealed V1a B0 streams (screen/efficiency_s{seed}), not re-run

parents: the 342 frozen V1a formal screen parents (formal/freeze.json)
noise_note: Same semantic keys as V1a (query, training seed, sampling seed 0, proposal number, cascade/joint group), so proposal j of a new arm starts from the same noise as proposal j of the sealed arm with the same program.
checkpoints: frozen V1a generators bound in formal/freeze.json (event_s*, geometry_s*, joint_s*)
cost_accounting: Budgets are charged at each arm's actual logical cost (25*w_g + 25*w_h for A0-25+25, 25 for B0-25), never at a nominal 50.

primary.statistic: normalized log-budget joint best-reference recall AUC (V1a definition), parent-paired difference, mean over training seeds within parent

interpretation.lower_bound_above_zero: Under this control, 'joint generation is cheaper per network call' still holds.
interpretation.otherwise: V1a's B0 budget advantage can be explained by the number of integration steps and cannot be credited to joint generation.

secondary.method: task R analysis A on the completed-candidate axis (xtbflow.v1.reanalysis count_prefix + paired_difference); censoring, seed aggregation and coverage flag as in configs/v1a_r/reanalysis.json

descriptive.table: five-arm-format rows (recall and completed candidates at budgets 4/8/16/32/64, AUC, event AUC) for A0-25+25 and B0-25 next to the sealed A0 and B0

sources.sealed_count_streams: task R extract streams.jsonl.gz (sha256 recorded in docs/evidence/v1a_r/extract_manifest.json)
sources.new_reports: v1a-n run root screen/nfe_s{seed}.json and .candidates.jsonl, produced by scripts/v1a_stream_evaluate.py
